item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is materially closer to the frozen contract and has much tighter scope, though it still needs correction before merge. A adds expressly forbidden public association APIs and duplicate multipart/request machinery.","reasons":["B provides the exact Upload signature and directly reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\", while A introduces NewFileWithFields and six unrelated public association options.","B shares option handling, request construction, and response decoding through one internal path. A bypasses Add and duplicates its Raw.Do and response-decoding logic, creating drift risk.","A directly violates the instruction not to add association fields and even documents those options as applying to Add although Add ignores their form values.","B's implementation is easier to bring into compliance: leave Add unchanged and have Upload call Add with the replayable *bytes.Reader returned by NewFile."],"risks_a":["Upload does not route through FilesService.Add as required.","Adds forbidden WithFile*ID APIs and expands filesOptions and multipartbody solely to support them.","New association options silently do nothing when passed to Add despite comments claiming otherwise, creating misleading API behavior."],"risks_b":["Add now eagerly consumes and buffers every caller-supplied body, violating the requirement to preserve its existing behavior and potentially increasing memory use for custom streaming uploads.","Upload calls the private add helper rather than the existing public Add method, contrary to the explicit routing requirement.","Tests omit explicit empty-filename, nil-content, and source-reader-error cases, and replace the original Add test while dropping some method/path assertions."]}
